items.claim: This unit's two seams both rest on genuine frame-owner and speaker changes rather than on the parashah marks that merely corroborate them, and the verse-19 voice question is disclosed rather than resolved past what the bytes support.
items.evidence: The opening seam is a fresh collective addressee replying to Jeremiah, and the closing seam is Jeremiah resuming as narrated speaker under a fresh narrative verb at Jer.44.20; the setumah before Jer.44.15 and the petuchah closing Jer.44.19 are disclosed only as tier-3 texture, never as drivers. The verse-19 speaker question is handled carefully: the WEB text's own lead-in naming the women as speakers is disclosed as an English-side translational reading distinct from the Hebrew, which opens the verse on the conjunction 've-khi' with no narrative verb of speech restarting there, so the whole reply is correctly kept as one span rather than cut on an attribution the Hebrew itself does not mark. The rejected alternative directly engages this same tension rather than dodging it.

items.claim: The closing disclosure's claim that the recurring address tag 'widens' at its far end to add the women is contradicted by this unit's own quoted Hebrew, which already names the women in the tag at its own opening verse.
items.evidence: This unit's own boundary prose quotes the opening tag at Jer.44.20 as addressed 'al ha-gvarim ve-al ha-nashim ve-al kol ha'am', concerning the men and concerning the women and concerning all the people, so the women are already explicitly named there. The closing disclosure then describes the recurring tag at Jer.44.24 as reopening with the women 'added', which misstates the pattern: only the grammatical shape of the appositive changes between the two sites (an unqualified three-part list at Jer.44.20 versus a kol-qualified two-part list at Jer.44.24), not the women's presence, which is constant across both. Given how much weight this book's recurring formulas carry for seam arguments, a recurrence claim needs to describe what the bytes actually changed. Secondarily, the unit_type 'judgment_oracle' is applied to a stretch this unit's own prose says opens with no messenger formula and no fresh koh-amar; that operative-category basis is stated in the boundary prose but not carried into the closing disclosure sentence, unlike the neighboring whole-chapter unit at Jer.45.1-45.5, which places its own operative-category basis there correctly.

items.claim: Both seams rest on genuine discourse-imperative and header onsets, the live paragraph fold at Jer.44.25 is correctly disclosed as tier-4 only, and the digit-bearing sweeps cited for the divine-title form and the paseq count both check exactly against the inventories.
items.evidence: This unit opens on a fresh 'shim'u' discourse imperative naming the women beside the men and closes where a differently-shaped, date-internal header addressed to Baruch personally opens the next unit; the rejected alternative (cutting at the repeated 'lakhen shim'u devar YHWH' refrain inside the span) is genuine and is correctly rejected because no narrative verb of speech reopens there. The WEB paragraph fold inside Jer.44.25 is disclosed as tier-4 metadata only, matching the staged folded text exactly (continuation_paragraphs=1 at that verse and nowhere else in this unit's span). The adonai-skeleton sweep (11 of 13 verses, point-aware against the two courtly sites) and the two paseq segs at Jer.44.26 both check exactly against the disclosure inventory.

items.claim: This unit's whole-chapter cap is disclosed exactly as required, but its closing sentence's claim that the unit 'closes on the neum-YHWH formula' misstates the formula's position: the tag sits mid-verse, and the chapter's own last clause is the escape promise that follows it.
items.evidence: Jer.45.5 reads, per this unit's own Hebrew, through 'ki hineni mevi ra'ah al kol basar ne'um YHWH' and then continues 've-natati lekha et nafshekha le-shalal al kol ha-meqomot asher telekh sham': the ne'um-YHWH tag falls before the final clause promising Baruch's life, not at the verse's or the chapter's own end. A comparable mid-verse-versus-closing-tag distinction is drawn carefully elsewhere in this same cluster (the melekh-signature at Jer.46.18 is read as naming the oath's speaker mid-verse rather than trailing it as a closing tag, and the neum-YHWH at Jer.46.23 is read as sitting before the locust comparison rather than closing the verse), so the same positional care was available here. The cap disclosure itself is exemplary: confidence held at medium_low, the frontier flag set, and an explicit capped, low-granularity sentence naming the rejected verse-4 split; this challenge concerns only the formula-position claim in the closing sentence.

items.claim: The double-header opening is correctly kept as one unit absent any intervening addressee change between the nations rubric and Egypt's own header, and the neum-YHWH at Jer.46.5 is correctly read as corroboration rather than a driver since no fresh tier-1 onset follows it.
items.evidence: This unit treats the asher-hayah nations rubric at Jer.46.1 and the lamed-initial Egypt header at Jer.46.2 as sequential, distinct devices rather than conflating them; the exclusivity sweep for the rubric shape (one of only four verses, sweep of 4 verses) checks exactly against the four-site inventory. The neum-YHWH at Jer.46.5 is explicitly withheld from driving a cut because no fresh tier-1 onset follows at Jer.46.6, which continues the same flight imperative, correct application of the closure-corroboration-only rule. The la-adonai construction at Jer.46.10 is quoted at the byte tier without an unverified book-wide count, properly avoiding an uncited universal claim. The rejected alternative (cutting immediately after the header) directly engages a real rival rather than a strawman.

items.claim: The header at Jer.46.13 is correctly disclosed as its own device rather than forced into any of the book's three canonical word-event shapes, and the melekh-signature at Jer.46.18 is correctly read as naming the oath's speaker mid-verse rather than functioning as a trailing closure tag.
items.evidence: This unit withholds the Jer.46.13 header from all three canonical word-event shapes on byte grounds (built on the verb spoke rather than came or was), which is accurate rather than assimilated to a shape it does not match. The melekh-signature exclusivity sweep (one of only three sites, sweep of 3 verses) matches the book's three-site inventory exactly. The back seam, a fresh direct address to the daughter who dwells in Egypt at Jer.46.19, is a genuine addressee shift, and this unit correctly stops before it. The declared heuristic flags on this unit's universal-sounding language are, on inspection, legitimate digit-paired or self-scoped statements, not defects waved through.

items.claim: This span is a genuine inclusio bracketed by matching direct-address vocatives to the daughter of Egypt at its own open and close, and it correctly declines to let either the tier-3 mark closing the opening verse or the mid-verse neum-YHWH at Jer.46.23 drive an internal cut.
items.evidence: Jer.46.19 opens on 'yoshevet bat Mitsrayim' and Jer.46.24 closes on 'bat Mitsrayim', a genuine bracketing device disclosed as an inclusio rather than as independent boundary evidence. The setumah closing Jer.46.19 is correctly held to tier-3 corroboration only, not treated as licensing a split at the opening verse; the neum-YHWH at Jer.46.23 is correctly identified as sitting mid-verse before the locust comparison, not as a closing tag. The rejected alternative directly engages the closing mark as the strongest case for an internal cut and explains why addressee continuity through the closing verse defeats it, rather than dismissing a weaker rival.

items.claim: Both of this two-verse span's seams rest on genuine addressee shifts rather than on formula repetition or marks alone, and the divine-title stack sweep it cites checks exactly against the inventory.
items.evidence: This unit opens on a distinct divine pronouncement naming Amon of No, Pharaoh, and Egypt's gods and kings, a fresh judgment target following the daughter-of-Egypt inclusio's own close at Jer.46.24, and ends where the address shifts completely to Jacob as covenant servant at Jer.46.27, a shift correctly noted as unbridged by any continuity marker. The full divine-title stack sweep (elsewhere counted at 32 verses, sweep of 32 verses) matches the inventory exactly. The unexpected restoration clause inside Jer.46.26 is disclosed as internal texture rather than promoted into its own boundary, consistent with holding the line against sub-unit atomizing.
